title: Dengue Vaccination in Children and Adolescents: Current Evidence, Safety, and Future Directions
content: Background: Dengue is an expanding mosquito-borne disease and a growing global health threat. Its four serotypes, changing epidemiology, and complex immune responses make vaccine development particularly challenging. This review examines dengue vaccines, with emphasis on children and adolescents. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through September 2026. Clinical trials, observational studies, reviews, surveillance reports, and guidelines addressing dengue immunopath-ogenesis, vaccine development, efficacy, immunogenicity, safety, effectiveness, or implementation were considered. Evidence was assessed with attention to pediatric populations, age, baseline serostatus, infecting serotype, and duration of protection. Results: CYD-TDV provides moderate protection, but long-term follow-up identified an increased risk of hospitalized or severe dengue in seronegative recipients, making pre-vaccination screening central to its use. TAK-003 protects children and adolescents against virologically confirmed and hospitalized dengue, although efficacy varies by serotype and serostatus; protection against DENV-3 and DENV-4 in seronegative recipients remains uncertain. Butantan-DV has shown efficacy across pediatric age groups and baseline serostatus categories after a single dose, but the absence of DENV-3 and DENV-4 cases limited serotype-specific estimates. TV003/TV005 and other plat-forms broaden the pipeline, though pediatric efficacy evidence remains limited. No validated correlate of protection is available. Affordability, equitable access, surveillance, and caregiver confidence remain important implementation challenges. Conclusion: Dengue vaccines mark important progress, but their benefits and risks depend on age, serostatus, and circulating serotypes. Long-term, serotype-specific evaluation and post-marketing surveillance are needed. Next-generation vaccines, clear communication, and sustainable access will be essential to achieve durable, equitable protection for children.
